transcript.text: My Shark cordless battery got really hot on charge last night and this morning it looks puffed up, the plastic case has split at the seam a bit. Can I still use it till a new one comes? It's the IZ201UK.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A swollen, very hot or chemical-smelling battery can catch fire. Stop using and charging it now, unplug the charger, and if it is safe to move put it somewhere non-flammable away from anything that could burn. Don't puncture, squeeze or try to open the battery, and don't put it in the household bin — take it to a battery recycling point. No, please don't use or charge it until it has been looked at. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
Ok, understood. It's currently leaning against the kitchen cupboards next to the tea towels, and it has a faint chemical smell. Where should I put it right now?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Switch off and unplug the charger at the wall, and if the battery isn't hot, hissing or smoking, move the vacuum to a hard surface that can't burn, ideally outside on concrete or a patio, well away from the tea towels, the house and people. Don't charge or use it again. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
